speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis with possible underlying inflammatory arthritis. The combination of lateral wrist/thumb pain exacerbated by infant holding, radiation to the elbow, and a positive family history for rheumatoid arthritis suggests an overuse injury (De Quervain's) potentially superimposed on or confused with an inflammatory process. I recommend requesting the following tests: REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid Factor, Anti-CCP; REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound_Wrist_right.
